description: Philippine dangerous-drug (S2) and controlled-precursor status by generic, from the Dangerous Drugs Board's consolidated schedules and Board Regulations. Generics not listed here follow their FDA Philippines registration classification (Rx / OTC / HR). Not legal advice; confirm with PDEA and the DDB.

alprazolam.rx_form: PDEA S-2 license required. Oral FDA-registered Philippine Schedule 4 preparations: ordinary prescription in triplicate (BR 1 s.2014 Sec. 4(4)(a)); other forms: DOH Special Prescription Form (yellow) (Sec. 31(2)). No refill; up to a 30-day supply, 60 days for epilepsy and dystonia (Sec. 31(6)(d)-(e)). Until June 30, 2027, S-2 licensed practitioners may use an ordinary prescription in triplicate instead of the special form (one dangerous drug per prescription, "NO REFILL", up to 30 days; 60 days for Philippine Schedule 4 drugs in epilepsy and dystonia) (BR 10 s.2025, extended by BR 5 s.2026).

ammonium-chloride-chlorphenamine-guaifen.rx_form: FDA-registered oral preparations are exempt from all DDB regulatory requirements except registration and licensing of the importer, exporter and manufacturer; prescription and dispensing follow FDA rules (BR 1 s.2014 Sec. 4(5)). Parenteral preparations are not covered by this exemption (Sec. 4(2)(c)(i)); prescribing a drug preparation containing a controlled chemical otherwise requires a PDEA S-2 license (Sec. 6(3)).
ammonium-chloride-chlorphenamine-guaifen.notes: BR 1 s.2014 Sec. 6(14)-(15): preparations with norephedrine/phenylpropanolamine 25 mg or below that are classified over-the-counter may be advertised to the public and distributed as samples; the S-2 license fee schedule (Sec. 6) likewise excludes them. The precursor exemption for oral FDA-registered preparations applies to combinations as well (BR 1 s.2014 Sec. 4(5)).

carisoprodol-paracetamol.notes: Newly listed: the DDB list dates its 1971 Schedule IV entry 6 December 2025; UN scope changes are adopted under BR 1 s.2020. BR 1 s.2014 Sec. 4(2)(a) lets the Board exempt a Schedule 4/5 preparation from specific controls only if it is non-parenteral, contains one dangerous drug, the drug cannot be readily recovered, and the exemption serves a medical purpose; no exemption is listed for this combination.
review: Carisoprodol was added to 1971 Schedule IV on the DDB list dated 6 December 2025; registered products may still carry their earlier Rx classification. Confirm the PDEA/FDA implementation date.
